business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global App Store Optimization and Multilingual Organic Search

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK-Cayman Islands Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA, in force 2010)
OECD Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to the Cayman Islands by the UK)
US-Cayman Islands Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) for FATCA compliance
Cayman Islands participation in the OECD/G20 BEPS Inclusive Framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2022 Revision); Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2023 Revision); Proceeds of Crime Act (2020 Revision); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act (2023); Tax Information Authority Act (2020 Revision); and the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority Guidance Notes on AML/CFT.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the individual's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for UK and other Hague Convention member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or recent financial institution statement proving commercial of the applicant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution holding the applicant's accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating from a Hague member state) or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each director and beneficial owner (utility bill or equivalent, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, municipal authority, or financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if issued in a Hague member state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney or engagement letter appointing the Cayman registered agent for pre-incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for UK and other Hague member countries)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and counterparties against the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury consolidated financial sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Cayman Islands Sanctions List, together with enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as required by the Cayman AML/CFT Regulations and Financial Reporting Authority guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry eServices Portal (Company Name Clearance and Reservation module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English or any Latin-script language; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into English for the register. The name must include the permissible suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must not be misleading in its transliterated English form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Anything implying connection with the Crown or a foreign government
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, attaching relevant evidence or regulatory consent for any restricted word. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may apply for an administrative reconsideration or, as a final step, commence judicial review proceedings in the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry provided the exempted company maintains a physical registered office in the Cayman Islands through a licensed corporate services provider; no requirement for the company to have a staffed operational presence in the Islands.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% annual likelihood) for a non-regulated app growth agency; moderately higher (25-40%) if the company later becomes subject to CIMA licensing or receives an AML/CFT review triggered by EMI or merchant account applications.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies Act (2022 Revision)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation fee for exempted company (authorized share capital not exceeding US$50,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies Act (2022 Revision); CI$870 equivalent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and registered agent / corporate secretary fees – first year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard exempted company maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-incorporation due diligence and UBO verification fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate services provider or approved KYC vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per entity file; includes OFAC, UK, EU, UN, and Cayman sanctions/PEP screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of CDD bundle (passports, proof of address, power of attorney)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cayman Islands legal opinion for pre-incorporation compliance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for exempted company formation legal opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership transparency register – initial filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act (2023)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act (2023 Revision) of the Cayman Islands (a British Overseas Territory of the United Kingdom), sections 13 and 181-190; Tax Concessions Act (2023 Revision), section 6
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry of the Cayman Islands, Grand Cayman KY1-1101 (eServices portal: generalregistry.gov.ky)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 189 upon filing of the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Exempted Company application) with the Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked-account requirement. Standard authorized capital is USD 50,000 divided into 50,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00; the initial government fee of approximately USD 1,000 applies to authorized capital up to USD 50,000, with annual renewal fees thereafter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company's registration as an exempted company under the Companies Act (2023) of the Cayman Islands, with the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed, be ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscriber share allotment be approved; that the office of the licensed corporate services provider in Grand Cayman be adopted as the registered office; that the directors named in the register of directors be appointed; and that the Chief Executive Officer and Corporate Secretary be appointed to office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that such officers be authorized to open banking and EMI accounts, execute client and vendor agreements, and file statutory returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint licensed registered office provider and corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Trust and corporate services provider licensed by the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Cayman formation agent holding a registered office consent; execute the engagement letter, complete CIMA-compliant KYC/AML due diligence, and instruct the agent to prepare the memorandum and articles.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter and corporate formation instructions
Certified passport copies of subscribers and directors
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-supply corrected KYC documents or address-proof within CIMA guidance; notarize or re-certify any rejected identification before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain name clearance and execute constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Grand Cayman
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name (e.g., 'Name Ltd.') for availability verification, then execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association with the subscribers' signatures in the presence of a notary or via the Registry's eForm digital signature module.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as inactive or reserved, resubmit with a revised name or file a statutory declaration that the proposed name is not identical to an existing registered name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation documents with the Registrar and pay government fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies via the eServices portal of the Cayman Islands General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Memorandum and Articles, the consent to act as registered office, and the exempted company statement; pay the approximate USD 1,000 filing fee electronically; the Registry stamps the documents and triggers issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Fully executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of the registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the Registry requisition within 14 calendar days by filing amended schedules or clarifications; if the filing is deemed withdrawn, re-file with fresh signatures and fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and verify exempted status
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 189 and confirm the company number, date of incorporation, authorized share capital, and exempted company classification against the instruction sheet.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Registry acknowledgment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any particular (name, capital, or status) is wrongly stated, apply to the Registrar for rectification in accordance with section 255 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold first board meeting and complete post-incorporation governance onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and registered office provider/corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, open the register of members and register of directors at the registered office, issue share certificates, and apply to the Minister of Finance for a tax exemption undertaking under section 6 of the Tax Concessions Act to secure 20 years (renewable to 50) of direct tax exemption.
required_dossiers: First board resolutions (adopting share allotment, registered office, and officer appointments)
Register of members and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-file any defective register within the correction period; if the tax undertaking is refused, reapply with revised dividend and corporate purpose details within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a non-resident offshore exempted company; if a physical place of business is later established in the Cayman Islands, the Department of Commerce and Investment (DCI) Trade and Business Licensing Unit is the competent authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required at formation for ASO/SEO localization agency services; a Trade and Business License under the Trade and Business Licensing Act (2023 Revision) would only be triggered by a physical Cayman office or local client-facing presence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full EIA or environmental registration is triggered because the company conducts purely administrative digital marketing services with no fixed industrial installation, land disturbance, or discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core business; if an office is opened, commercial waste must be handled under the Litter and Solid Waste Act (2023 Revision), with zero VOC and zero wastewater discharge thresholds applicable to any leased serviced office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: None required at incorporation. If staff occupy commercial premises, the employer must obtain a fire safety certificate under the Cayman Islands Fire Services regulations, confirm structural load compliance through the local building code, and maintain workplace health-and-safety clearance; remote workers require employer liability insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); online portal: GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk) and HMRC Online Services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman Exempted Company trading in the UK must register for Corporation Tax within 3 months of commencing business if it has a UK permanent establishment; application via HMRC Form CT41G or online to obtain a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). For VAT, a non-UK established business must register for VAT through HMRC's non-established business route using Form VAT1 (online via Government Gateway) before making the first taxable supply, with no registration threshold. If the company has no UK PE and makes no UK taxable supplies, no UK tax ID is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK has no check-the-box regime. A foreign entity may elect to apply the UK's unilateral treaty tie-breaker or make a claim for non-residence. For hybrid mismatch rules (TIOPA 2010 Part 6TA), the Cayman Exempted Company is generally treated as opaque and no transparency election is permitted. Elections are available to disapply the CFC rules where appropriate (e.g., for exempt activities) and to allocate profits to a UK PE under the authorised OECD approach.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) and import/export duties under the UK Global Tariff
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 annual taxable turnover for UK-established businesses; non-UK established (non-resident) businesses must register from the first taxable supply (no threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no mandatory B2B e-invoicing. Making Tax Digital (MTD) requires VAT-registered businesses to keep digital records and submit VAT returns via HMRC-recognised software through application programming interfaces (APIs). Paper/PDF e-invoices are permitted, subject to the VAT (Invoicing) Regulations 2003.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods exported to non-UK destinations, 0% VAT applies if the exporter keeps evidence of export within the required time and the goods are supplied to a person outside the UK. For cross-border services (SEO/ASO and localization), B2B supplies to a recipient who belongs outside the UK fall outside the scope of UK VAT (place of supply is the customer's country), so no UK VAT is charged; the UK supplier must obtain and preserve two pieces of non-conflicting evidence of the customer's identity, belonging and business status (e.g., VAT registration number, customer's tax ID or corporate registry extract). No FX repatriation deadline applies in the UK; funds may be received through Wise B2B or Payoneer without exchange-control restriction. Any input VAT attributable to exports/outside-scope supplies is recoverable under the normal rules (subject to partial exemption de minimis).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CDS/CHIEF) for goods exports
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (for goods and services)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export
Bank statement or payment processor FX receipt (Wise B2B or Payoneer payout report) as evidence of receipt
Inward Remittance Certificate (where local exchange-control rules impose one, otherwise not required in the UK)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may open a formal review or verification of any zero-rating or outside-scope claim. For insufficient export evidence, the output VAT is clawed back with interest from the date of supply, with a penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded for deliberate conduct or 30% for careless/inaccurate declarations. For services, failure to retain valid customer evidence leads to VAT assessment and similar penalties. Fraudulent claims can result in criminal prosecution, disqualification, and repayment of any VAT refunded. The assessment period is generally 4 years, extended to 20 years for fraud or loss of HMRC revenue.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England, in coordination with H.M. Treasury and HM Revenue & Customs. The UK does not maintain a standalone Foreign Exchange Administration. FX-related regulation of banks and payment institutions is exercised by the Bank of England and, for conduct purposes, the Financial Conduct Authority. Sanctions and counter-terrorist financing enforcement is led by H.M. Treasury through the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Sterling is fully convertible for current and capital account purposes. The UK has no exchange control legislation requiring prior approval for inbound capital injections, dividend remittances, or profit repatriation. Non-resident Cayman exempted companies may hold GBP or foreign-currency accounts and move funds freely, subject to sanctions screening, AML/CTF checks, and tax reporting. Profits derived by a Cayman company will generally be outside the UK corporate tax net unless the company has UK permanent establishment or receives UK-source income; profit remittance from a UK subsidiary to a Cayman parent would not be blocked, but withholding and transfer-pricing rules must be considered separately.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The UK imposes no export proceeds surrender rules and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts and cross-border service fees may be retained in the invoiced currency. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds to the UK. However, receipts must be accurately recorded for corporate tax, VAT, and HMRC audit purposes, and the supporting banking transactions must carry appropriate purpose codes to satisfy sanctions and financial crime screening obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account and FX settlement account
Treasury and FX clearing account for non-resident corporate entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for Wise B2B and Payoneer. These FCA-regulated EMI/payment institutions accept remote onboarding for non-resident Cayman exempted companies and support SWIFT, local clearings, and multi-currency treasury balances. Legal constraints: EMIs are not licensed banks, do not provide credit, are not covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme, and must safeguard client funds. The EMI rail is suitable for operational agency fee flows and localization supplier disbursements, while long-term capital escrow and FX hedging should be anchored in a tier-1 bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: UK tier-1 banks do not statutorily require physical attendance of directors, but practically most request a video interview for non-resident clients and may require a UK address or UK-resident director for high-risk or offshore structures. A Cayman exempted company with non-resident directors will face enhanced due diligence; fully remote account opening is more common with fintech EMIs, while full-service UK banks often reserve the right to require a meeting at a UK branch or with an international banking representative before onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Islands jurisdiction flag due to offshore financial centre and public transparency expectations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman Registered Office Certificate, Certificate of Good Standing from the Cayman Registrar, completed economic substance notification or exemption confirmation, board resolution approving UK bank account, and a clear explanation of the commercial substance of the ASO/SEO agency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt or low-substance structure of the Cayman Exempted Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate register extract, signed beneficial ownership register, organisational chart showing active management, commercial client contracts, app store agency agreements, marketing deliverables, and evidence of actual operational expenditure in the localization agency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership or complex shareholding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO declaration naming all natural persons with control, passport copies with proof of address, corporate custody chain certificates, and explanation of no bearer shares. If a trust acts as shareholder, provide a legal opinion or trust deed summary confirming beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for initial deposit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the funding shareholder, signed and dated share subscription or loan agreement, board minutes approving the capital injection, investor invoices, and, if available, audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements for the Cayman company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media screening hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent global sanctions/PEP screening report, negative-media search results, professional reference letters, counterparty due diligence, and a written self-declaration explaining any unrelated names or deviations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound funding should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the Cayman company's own bank to the UK account. The transfer instruction must show the legal name of the Cayman company, the account number and BIC, and an LEI where held. Use ISO 20022 or bank-specific purpose code equivalent to 'equity injection' or 'intra-group capital contribution' and include a board resolution reference in the remittance field. The full dossier should be pre-cleared with the UK receiving bank: certificate of incorporation, register of directors, UBO declaration, source-of-funds evidence, and an explanation of the app growth agency business. For amounts exceeding risk thresholds, provide board minutes and signed subscription documents to ensure the deposit is classified as capital rather than unidentified credit. Due to the UK's absence of exchange controls, no HMRC or Bank of England approval is required, but the funds remain subject to sanctions screening and may be frozen if any name on the wire is sanctioned.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border service payments to localization vendors, app analytics platforms, and subcontractors, use SWIFT MT103 for non-UK counterparties; use Faster Payments or CHAPS for UK domestic counterparties; and use SEPA CT for euro payments within the EEA. Commercial letters of credit are generally unsuitable for pure ASO/SEO service disbursements, but a standby letter of credit may be requested by a large client or supplier. Wise B2B and Payoneer act as efficient conversion and clearing rails for lower-value recurring payments, providing local USD and EUR settlement, while large strategic or capital payments should be cleared via tier-1 bank MT103 instructions with exact purpose codes and supporting vouchers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (GBP/USD/EUR, and GBP vs Asia-Pacific app-store settlement currencies) with a UK-authorised bank under an ISDA Master Agreement
Market-standard non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies in app-store remittance corridors where local currency convertibility or delivery restrictions apply
Cross-currency swaps for long-term treasury exposure on multi-currency balances, limited to genuine commercial hedging and not speculative trading
FX swap/rollover structures for managing short-term funding mismatches across the agency's multi-currency operational accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Annual Declaration and Government Fees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (General Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for all existing exempted companies; new companies pay pro-rated fees at incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee if paid after 31 January, escalating by an additional 10% per month (capped at 100%); persistent non-payment may lead to administrative strike-off and forfeiture of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Department for International Tax Cooperation via the Registrar's online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (typically 31 December for calendar-year entities); must be filed annually even if no relevant activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalties up to CI$5,000 plus daily default penalties; repeated failure may trigger court action and potential strike-off of the company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a standard Cayman Exempted Company unless it is licensed under banking, trust, insurance, or mutual fund regulations, or is listed on a stock exchange; otherwise the audit is voluntary
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP commonly adopted; no mandatory local statutory GAAP for private exempted companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cayman law does not mandate an annual UBO confirmation filing; however, the Beneficial Ownership Register must be maintained (on-site or with the registered agent) and updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; the Register is available for inspection by prescribed supervisory authorities on demand

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 per annum (voluntary audit for a small agency)

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: Cayman Islands: 0% on all domestic and foreign income; United Kingdom: main rate 25% from 1 April 2023 (small profits rate 19% below £50,000; marginal relief 21.5% between £50,001–£250,000).
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No UK statutory tax holiday for ASO/SEO agencies; UK R&D tax relief (SME 86% deduction; merged scheme from 1 April 2024); Patent Box 10%; Cayman exempted company endures zero Cayman CIT and no DST equivalent; UK Digital Services Tax 2% applies only to specified social media/search/advertising-linked turnover and not to agency fees; potential effective rate 0% if no UK PE and no DPT applies.
